evidence.body: [e002:f01] ](https:// * [Beige Book: Eight of 12 districts report growth as wage pressures pick up](https:// * [Baker Hughes US rig count holds steady at 607. [e002:f05] The small-cap gain showed how far the recovery had spread, even with chip stocks still weighing on the Nasdaq. #### The dollar was mixed The USD was strongest against the Australian dollar, with AUDUSD down 0.15% to 0.6628, and weakest against the Swiss franc, with USDCHF down 0.56% to 0.8309. [e002:f08] Buyers stepped in after a steep morning selloff At the session lows, the S&P 500 was down about 231 points, or 3.2%, and the Nasdaq Composite was down roughly 1,090 points, or 4.6%. [e002:f09] Buyers stepped in during the afternoon, and by the close those losses had narrowed to 18 points and 148 points, respectively. [e002:f10] The Russell 2000 turned positive and finished up 0.71% as the rebound broadened. * S&P 500 — 7,182.78, −0.25% * Nasdaq Composite — 23,585.80, −0.62% * Russell 2000 — 2,704.06, +0.71% * Nasdaq 100 — 26,046.90, −0.64% in the late-session snapshot * Dow — 50,182.95, +0.33% ### Chip stocks still lagged Nvidia was down nearly 9% in the morning, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was off more than 7%. [e002:f11] Two sessions after Jensen Huang’s return sparked a relief rally, investors are still asking how much profit all that AI spending will generate and how long it will take. [](https:// #### European stocks closed lower Europe closed with the Nasdaq 100 still down nearly 4%. [e002:f12] Spain and Italy led the losses. [](https:// * Germany’s DAX — 24,702.14, −1.26% * France’s CAC 40 — 7,980.57, −0.75% * U.K.’s FTSE 100 — 10,426.95, −0.38% * Spain’s IBEX 35 — 18,635.80, −2.00% * Italy’s FTSE MIB — 47,249.14, −1.81% #### The news behind the moves **Core inflation picked up as real spending stalled.** October core PCE rose 0.3% on the month, as expected. [e002:f13] The annual rate increased to 3.3% from 3.1%, above the 3.2% forecast. [e002:f14] The Fed has inflation still running above target and a more recent reading on household demand that shows less momentum than the third-quarter GDP report. [](https:// **GDP was revised higher and claims fell.** Third-quarter growth was revised to 4.3% annualized from 3.4%, above the 3.5% forecast, with investment and consumer spending driving the revision. [e002:f15] Initial jobless claims dropped to 189K and continuing claims fell to 1.697M. [e002:f16] October durable goods orders rose just 0.2% versus 0.6% expected, but core capital goods orders beat expectations with a 1.2% gain. [](https:// **The Beige Book showed modest growth and firmer wages.** Eight of 12 Fed districts reported slight to moderate growth, down from nine in the previous report.

evidence.title: Nasdaq 100 Analysis: Uncertainty Returns to NDX Following Tariff Announcements
evidence.body: [e003:f01] After the strong rebound seen at the beginning of the week, when the index advanced nearly **6.0%** during Monday's session, the following two sessions ahead of the Thanksgiving market closure have reflected a decline of roughly **3.0%**, highlighting that uncertainty is once again becoming an important feature of the index's price action. [e003:f02] Part of the confidence that had returned to the market thanks to **Nvidia** at the start of the week has begun to fade following recent announcements regarding potential tariffs from the United States. [e003:f03] Added to this is the possibility of a more aggressive **Federal Reserve**, which continues to act as a constant source of uncertainty for markets. [e003:f04] Together, these factors have once again complicated the recovery in sentiment and could continue highlighting a period of indecision around the **Nasdaq 100** in the short term. [! [e003:f05] ** Although the bullish move around the **Nasdaq 100** was quite significant at the start of the week due to the relief generated by **Jensen Huang's** return as president of **Nvidia**, that recovery in confidence failed to remain consistent. [e003:f06] In fact, during today's session the index fell nearly **4.5%**, a move that now appears linked to a new source of uncertainty for risk assets: the recent announcements of potential tariffs from the United States. [e003:f07] During the session, it became known that, following a trade investigation, the United States determined that at least **14 major economies**, including the **European Union** and **China**, maintain industrial policies that could distort global competition and negatively affect U.S. industry over the long term. [e003:f08] Tariffs of up to **20%** are being considered for the European Union and China, while economies such as **Japan**, **South Korea**, and **Taiwan** could face tariffs of around **15%**. [e003:f09] In fact, indicators such as the **Fear & Greed Index** continue to hover around **16 points**, reflecting an **"extreme fear"** environment and highlighting that investors remain cautious as new risks emerge for economic growth. ! [e003:f10] [Image 2](https:// Source: CNN The situation is particularly relevant for the **Nasdaq 100**, given the significant exposure many of its companies have to global supply chains. [e003:f11] Looking at the ten most influential companies within the Nasdaq, only **Apple (+0.3%)**, **SpaceX (+0.95%)**, and **Meta (+2.56%)** managed to post gains during the session, while the remaining components recorded notable declines, reflecting that confidence around the technology sector remains relatively fragile. ! [e003:f12] There is currently close to a **100% probability** that the Fed will raise rates again at the **December 9** meeting, taking the benchmark rate toward the **4.25%** area. [e003:f13] Markets had expected a reading of **3.2%**, but the official figure reached **3.3%**, reinforcing the view that inflationary pressures remain relevant within the U.S. economy. [e003:f14] At the same time, a higher interest-rate environment could increase borrowing costs, affect consumer spending, and reduce liquidity available for risk assets such as Nasdaq. [e003:f15] As a result, if new economic data or Fed commentary continue supporting a more aggressive central bank into year-end, indecision or even a new period of weakness could remain relevant around the **Nasdaq 100** over the coming weeks. #### **Nasdaq 100 Technical Forecast** ! [e003:f16] [Image 4](https:// Source: StoneX, Tradingview * **Bearish trend remains in place:**Since the first days of October, the **Nasdaq 100** has been developing a pattern of progressively lower highs and lower lows.

evidence.title: 米国経済の先行きに暗雲？FRBの追加利上げとデータセンター規制強化でAI投資ブームに急ブレーキのリスク【伊藤忠総研レポート】 2026年11月25日
evidence.body: [e005:f01] 長期金利の高止まりは、企業の資金調達コストの上昇や株式市場の調整を通じて、設備投資や個人消費の重しとなる見込み。 [e005:f02] さらに、データセンター規制強化によってAI投資が想定以上に減速し、米国経済が下振れるリスクにも警戒が必要である。 [e005:f03] 米金融政策見通し：2025年実施の予防的利下げの巻き戻しが進む 12月8～9日開催のFOMCでは、政策金利が0.25％pt引き上げられ、4.0～4.25％となると予想する。 [e005:f04] 10月のCPIではインフレの粘着性が引き続き確認されたことに加え、堅調な経済活動と雇用情勢が維持されていることから、追加利上げの必要性は高いと考えられる。 [e005:f05] なお、 FOMCでの議論への影響力が大きいウォラー理事は、11月の講演で0.5％ptの大幅利上げも選択肢に上ると言及した。 [e005:f06] その後、株価が大幅に下落し、長期金利もやや上昇したことで金融環境が悪化したことを踏まえれば、12月FOMCでは0.25％ptの利上げが多数派となるだろう。 [e005:f07] 12月FOMCでの議論は、 ①エネルギー高のインフレへの影響 、 ②堅調な景気がインフレ圧力を持続させる可能性 、 ③AIブームが調整されるリスク などが中心になると考えられる。 [e005:f08] ①エネルギー高については、2027年央にはインフレに及ぼす影響が弱まるとの見方が多いが、FRBが11月に公表した分析では、コロナ禍後は構造変化が起こり、原油価格のコアインフレへの波及度とインフレの持続性が高まったリスクが指摘されている。 [e005:f09] 他方、 金利上昇による資金調達コスト増を背景としたAI関連投資の収益性に対する懸念や、中間選挙での民主党勝利に伴うデータセンター規制の強化観測から、AIブームが調整局面に入り、景気が下押しされるリスクも議論されるだろう。 [e005:f10] 先行きについて当社は、「12月の利上げ後に様子見姿勢に移行する」との従来予想を修正し、2027年にも0.25％ptの追加利上げが実施され、政策金利は4.25～4.5％に達すると予想する。 [e005:f11] 追加利上げの時期は、金融引き締めの影響を見極めるため、2027年春頃になると見込むが、エネルギー高によるインフレリスクや物価上昇圧力の広がりが一段と強まれば、1月FOMCに前倒しされる可能性もある。 [e005:f12] 一方で、 AI関連株価の大幅下落などを契機に金融環境が急激に引き締まり、景気が過度に冷え込むリスクが強まれば、追加利上げが先送りされ、利下げへの転換が早まる可能性もあるだろう。 [e005:f13] 米景気見通し：高金利と規制がAI投資の勢いを抑制するリスク 米国経済の先行きをみると、AI関連の旺盛なインフラ需要と安定した雇用環境が下支えとなり、拡大基調を維持すると見込まれる。 [e005:f14] そのため、長期金利は高止まりが見込まれ、住宅市場の停滞を長期化させるだけでなく、企業の資金調達コスト増加や株式市場の調整を通じて設備投資および個人消費の重しとなる公算が大きい。 [e005:f15] すでに、10月中旬以降、金利上昇を受けてAI関連企業の資金調達環境に対する懸念がくすぶり続けている。 [e005:f16] 今後の実質GDP成長率は＋2％前後で一進一退の推移をたどる見込みである。

evidence.title: PCE Inflation Hits 3.8%. Strong GDP Growth Raises Odds of More Fed Hikes.
The Fed is likely to raise rates in December. What it means for your holiday spending
evidence.body: [e001:f01] What it means for your holiday spending](https:// * [Trump administration proposes rule that could curb ESG investing in 401(k)s](https:// * [CNBC’s Financial Advisor 100: Best financial advisors, top firms for 2026 ranked](https:// * [CNBC Elite Advisors: Top ultra-high net worth wealth management firms for 2026](https:// The central bank sets the federal funds rate, the interest rate at which banks borrow and lend to one another overnight. [e001:f02] When the Fed raises rates, borrowing becomes more expensive, helping to slow economic activity and ease inflation. [e001:f03] As the federal funds rate rises, so does the prime rate, which credit card issuers use as a benchmark. [e001:f04] Card rates typically adjust within one or two billing cycles after the Fed adjusts its policy. [e001:f05] Not only are Americans heading into the fourth quarter carrying a [record $1.29 trillion](https:// in credit card debt, but 66% of consumers with unsecured debt are still paying off last year’s holiday purchases, according to [a recent survey](https:// of 2,000 U.S. adults by National Debt Relief, a debt settlement firm. [e001:f06] “What’s particularly concerning is that many Americans are heading into this holiday season still paying off debt from the last one,” Peter Beaugard, chief revenue officer at National Debt Relief, said in a written statement. [e001:f07] “When holiday spending turns into debt that carries over year after year, it can create a cycle that becomes increasingly difficult to break.” With [affordability already stretched](https:// higher borrowing costs could put additional pressure on household budgets, though the impact is unlikely to be felt evenly, experts said. [e001:f08] “Higher-income households that pay their card balance in full won’t see any significant change in what ends up under the tree,” said Cristian deRitis, deputy chief economist at Moody’s Analytics. [e001:f09] As borrowing becomes more expensive and debt burdens grow, households may have little choice but to pull back on spending in the months ahead, experts say. [e001:f10] That may include holiday spending, though consumers may first opt to look for savings elsewhere, experts said. [e001:f11] “Some spending will be trimmed, but consumers will likely cut elsewhere before they cut gifts,” deRitis said. ## [](https:// loans and mortgage rates remain elevated Other borrowing costs are affected more indirectly by the central bank. [e001:f12] Even as new-car APRs hover above 7% and car prices remain elevated, December is traditionally a good time to buy a vehicle as dealers look to clear inventory before the end of the year, according to Ivan Drury, director of insights at Edmunds. [e001:f13] “Normally, waiting for December APR deals comes with a tradeoff: shrinking inventory of current-model-year vehicles, where discounts would provide the most value,” he said. [e001:f14] Auto loan interest rates remain near historic [highs](https:// — and could go even higher — while the average transaction price has climbed above $50,000. [e001:f15] Justin Sullivan | Getty Images Alternatively, 15- and 30-year fixed [mortgage rates](https:// don’t move with the Fed’s benchmark rate. [e001:f16] As a result, 30-year fixed mortgage rates have stayed above 7% since September, according to [Mortgage News Daily](https:// pushing the real estate sector into a[](https:// freeze](https:// !

evidence.title: If the Fed Raises Interest Rates Multiple Times in the Coming Months, Here’s What Billionaire Investor David Tepper Would Do
evidence.body: [e002:f01] By Bram Berkowitz – Nov 25, 2026 at 12:43PM EST Key Points Tepper closely watches the Federal Reserve's moves when determining his investment strategy. [e002:f02] Tepper's typical philosophy has been, "Don't fight the Fed." So caution may be the watchword now. [e002:f03] 10 stocks we like better › The Federal Reserve has already raised its benchmark overnight lending rate — the federal funds rate — once this year, and the market thinks it's only just getting started. [e002:f04] According to CME Group 's FedWatch tool, traders see a December hike as a near certainty as of this writing, with multiple hikes to follow in the first half of 2027 that would lift interest rates into a range of 4.50% to 4.75%. [e002:f05] For investors who expected the Fed to be dovish heading into 2026, that's a big shift. [e002:f06] One of those participants was billionaire investor David Tepper, who founded Appaloosa Management in 1993 and generated spectacular compounded gains of roughly 25% over 25 years. [e002:f07] Throughout his career, Tepper and his team have specialized in examining the movements of the country's central bank and the broader economy to determine their broader impact on the stock market and Appaloosa's investment strategy. [e002:f08] Tepper's rule: "Don't fight the Fed" Tepper's mantra dates back to at least 2010, when interest rates were at zero to stimulate the economy, and the Fed was pumping money into the economy through massive bond purchases. [e002:f09] That's because this increases liquidity and essentially creates what some economists call a "punchbowl" for the market. [e002:f10] Furthermore, in late 2022, when central banks began rapidly raising interest rates, Tepper said he was "leaning short" on stocks because the risk-reward proposition didn't make sense with so many central banks providing their playbook of economic tightening. [e002:f11] Higher yields also make bonds more competitive, meaning equities need to deliver higher returns for investors to take on the risk. [e002:f12] " That’s because not fighting the Fed means not selling stocks into an easing cycle, even though he also warned the Fed should not cut rates too much until inflation had made clear headway toward the Fed's 2% target. [e002:f13] With the Fed now hawkish, I would think Tepper's outlook has changed dramatically and that the investor prefers a risk-off approach into a rising-rate environment. [e002:f14] Fed Governor Christopher Waller recently said the Fed may need to raise rates by half a point in December. [e002:f15] Tepper's rule has worked for decades, and following it is more about reading the tea leaves than knowing exactly what the Fed will do. [e002:f16] They just revealed what they believe are the 10 best stocks for investors to buy right now, available when you join Stock Advisor.

evidence.title: The White House announced a raft of new tariffs on the same day inflation data came back at nearly twice the Fed’s target
evidence.body: [e003:f01] The White House has announced a litany of new tariffs targeting imports from 14 economies, including key trading partners such as China and the EU. [e003:f02] With consumers already stretched by an affordability crisis, the new duties come on the same day that the Bureau of Economic Analysis confirmed inflation hit 3.8%, according to the annual rate of the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, and nearly double the Federal Open Market Committee’s 2% goal. [e003:f03] Recommended Video The announcement has two important implications. [e003:f04] First, though the new duties would be imposed on foreign economies, previous tariff studies indicate that 90% of the increased prices are ultimately borne by U.S. businesses and, more often than not, their consumers. [e003:f05] The Fed, now led by Kevin Warsh, raised rates in September for the first time since July 2023, to a range of 3.75% to 4%, and meets again Dec. [e003:f06] Former Fed chairman Jerome Powell said that while tariffs represented a one-off price increase rather than broader inflationary factors, they nonetheless increased near-term inflation expectations. [e003:f07] As UBS chief economist Paul Donovan told clients today: “The concern is the impact on U.S. inflation, and thus U.S. interest rates.” And the Fed already has a data headache on its hands: The PCE increase to 3.8% compared with a year ago is nearly double the FOMC’s 2% target. [e003:f08] China faces a new 20% duty, and Vietnam, up to 35%, or 20% if it reaches a trade deal, according to Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, citing Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974. [e003:f09] Section 301 allows the U.S. to investigate foreign practices deemed unreasonable or discriminatory, or that burden or restrict U.S. commerce. [e003:f10] Both nations are among the top 10 importers to the U.S., accounting for 7.8% and 7.4% of imports, respectively, per Census Bureau data . [e003:f11] The European Union is also facing tariffs of 15%, while India is facing rates of up to 25%, or 17% in the event of a trade deal. [e003:f12] The new revenue-generating tariff action comes after the Supreme Court struck down Trump’s sweeping emergency tariffs in February, forcing the administration to refund roughly $100 billion of the $166 billion it had collected. [e003:f13] For most of the 14 economies, existing Section 301 duties count toward the new rate rather than being added on top. (China is the exception: Its 20% stacks on existing levies.) “In effect, it’ll look more like a top-up,” Greer told CNBC’s Squawk Box . [e003:f14] The New York Fed’s October survey of consumer expectations revealed that households expect inflation to be at 3.9% this time next year, and at 3.3% in three years’ time. [e003:f15] “The tariffs replace the previously announced Section 301 tariffs with a marginal incremental impact higher on goods prices but, moreover, set the table for further increases if negotiations break down,” Bradford Smith, portfolio manager at Janus Henderson Investors, told Fortune in a note. [e003:f16] “The announcement serves as a reminder that the Fed’s inflation fight is exacerbated by tariffs.

evidence.title: 米連邦準備制度理事会ベージュブック「8地域が緩やかな成長…物価圧力は依然」
evidence.body: [e004:f01] 米連邦準備制度理事会（Fed）が公表したベージュブックによると、12の連邦準備銀行管轄地域のうち8地域がわずかな、または緩やかな成長を示し、残り4地域はほぼ横ばいだった。 [e004:f02] 消費支出は大きな変化がなかったものの、価格への敏感さが高まり、非必需消費や自動車販売が減少、住宅用不動産市場も縮小した。 [e004:f03] 雇用は小幅に増加し、新規採用は退職者の補充に集中した。 [e004:f04] 賃金と福利厚生費の上昇ペースは前回報告より加速し、エネルギー・運輸・医療・保険・関税関連のコスト負担がある中でも、競争激化により消費者への転嫁には限界があった。 [e004:f05] 大半の地域は今後も緩やかな成長を予想した。 [e004:f06] 米連邦準備制度理事会（Fed）が25日（現地時間）に公表した景気動向報告書ベージュブックで、12の連邦準備銀行管轄地域のうち8地域がわずかな、または緩やかな成長を示したと明らかにした。 [e004:f07] 残り4地域はおおむね横ばいにとどまった。 [e004:f08] ただ物価負担が大きくなる中で価格に敏感になった消費者が非必需支出を減らす動きが現れ、自動車販売もやや鈍化した。 [e004:f09] 大半の企業が既存の人員規模を維持する中、新規採用は退職者の穴を埋める水準に集中した。 [e004:f10] 企業が採用拡大に依然として慎重な姿勢を示していることを意味する。 [e004:f11] 賃金と福利厚生費は緩やかに上昇し、上昇ペースは前回報告より加速した。 [e004:f12] 物価圧力はなかなか沈静化していない。 [e004:f13] ただ競争激化と消費者の価格敏感さのため、こうしたコストを販売価格にそのまま反映するのは難しかったと報告書は伝えた。 [e004:f14] 大半の地域は今後も経済活動がわずかな、または緩やかな拡大の流れを続けると見通した。 [e004:f15] 成長自体は維持されるものの、物価上昇圧力が同時に残る局面が当面続くとの観測だ。 [e004:f16] 今回の報告書は米連邦準備制度理事会（Fed）の金利判断の参考資料として使われる。

evidence.title: FRBベージュブック、12地区中8地区で景気拡大も物価高が重荷
evidence.body: [e005:f01] FRBが25日公表したベージュブックによると、全米12地区のうち8地区で景気が小幅から緩やかに拡大し、4地区は横ばいだった。 [e005:f02] 物価は幅広い業種でエネルギーや輸送、関税関連のコスト上昇が続き、緩やかに上昇。 [e005:f03] 消費者の価格敏感姿勢から企業の値上げは限定的で、個人消費はほぼ変化がなかった。 [e005:f04] 先行きも物価高が数カ月続くとの見方が示され、12月のFOMCに向けた討議資料となる。 [e005:f05] 米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）は25日、全米12地区の連邦準備銀行がまとめた景況報告（ベージュブック）を公表した。 [e005:f06] 景気は8地区で「小幅から緩やかな拡大」となり、4地区は横ばいだった。 [e005:f07] 物価上昇圧力は幅広い業種に及び、家計の支出はほぼ横ばいにとどまっている。 [e005:f08] 調査は16日までの情報を集約したもので、12月8、9両日に開く連邦公開市場委員会（FOMC）の討議資料として使われる。 [e005:f09] エネルギーや輸送、関税関連費用、保険料といったコストの増加が続いているとの声が幅広い業界から上がった。 [e005:f10] 原材料高もコストを押し上げているが、消費者の価格への警戒が強く、企業は十分な値上げに踏み切れていない状況だという。 [e005:f11] 先行きについても、今後数カ月にわたり支出と物価が上昇を続けるとの見方が示された。 [e005:f12] 需要面では、インフレの長期化を背景に家計の節約志向が強まり、個人消費は目立った変化がなかった。 [e005:f13] 労働需要は安定または増加しているとする業界が複数あった。 [e005:f14] FRBは今回の報告で、物価高が数カ月間続くとの認識をにじませた。 [e005:f15] 市場では、12月のFOMCで政策金利の据え置きを決めるとの見方が多い。 [e005:f16] 物価と雇用の両面をにらんだ慎重な運営が続く公算が大きい。
